topics.title: WATER SCARCITY AND THE NEED FOR WATER CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT

subtopics.title: Causes of Water Scarcity
subtopics.description: The text explains that water scarcity arises from over‑exploitation, excessive use, and unequal access to water, despite the abundance of freshwater from precipitation, surface runoff, and groundwater.

subtopics.title: Impact of Population Growth on Water Demand
subtopics.description: Large and growing populations increase domestic and agricultural water demand, leading to over‑exploitation of water resources for irrigation and food production.

subtopics.title: Agricultural Water Use and Irrigation
subtopics.description: Irrigated agriculture is the largest consumer of water; expanding irrigated areas for dry‑season agriculture over‑exploits groundwater, threatening food security.

subtopics.title: Industrial and Urban Water Consumption
subtopics.description: Industrialization and urbanization increase water and energy demands; industries use large amounts of water and rely on hydroelectric power, further stressing freshwater resources.

subtopics.title: Water Quality Issues and Pollution
subtopics.description: Even where water is abundant, pollution from domestic, industrial, chemical, pesticide, and fertilizer waste can render it hazardous, highlighting the need for quality management.

subtopics.title: Conservation and Management Strategies
subtopics.description: The chapter emphasizes the necessity of conserving and managing water resources to safeguard health, food security, livelihoods, and ecosystems, and to prevent ecological crisis.

topics.title: MULTI-PURPOSE RIVER PROJECTS AND INTEGRATED WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT

subtopics.title: What are dams and how do they help us in conserving and managing water?
subtopics.description: This subtopic discusses the role of dams in impounding rivers and rainwater for later irrigation, electricity generation, water supply, flood control, recreation, and fish breeding, illustrating their multi‑purpose nature.

subtopics.title: Classification of Dams
subtopics.description: Dams are classified according to structure, intended purpose, or height, and include features such as spillways or weirs that regulate water flow.

subtopics.title: Sringaverapura Water Harvesting System
subtopics.description: In the first century B.C., Sringaverapura near Allahabad had a sophisticated water harvesting system that channeled flood water from the Ganga, demonstrating early hydraulic engineering.

subtopics.title: Chandragupta Maurya Era Irrigation
subtopics.description: During Chandragupta Maurya’s reign, dams, lakes, and irrigation systems were extensively built, evidencing large‑scale water management in ancient India.

subtopics.title: Later Historical Water Structures
subtopics.description: Examples include Bhopal Lake (11th century), the tank in Hauz Khas, Delhi (14th century), and irrigation works in Kalinga, Nagarjunakonda, Bennur, and Kolhapur, illustrating continued hydraulic development.
